English: Ember Patch
A humble ring of stones, sheltered by animal hides, where the first embers of the sacred fire are kept alive by the faithful. A symbol of unity for the Baltic nomads.
Fire Ring
A reinforced fire ring of river stones and sturdy stakes, where tribes gather for rituals. The fires glow strengthens kinship and inspires reverence.
Torch Stand
An array of torch stands encircle the sacred fire, lighting the encampment at night and guiding the faithful to communal rites.
Flame Pavilion
A large, hide-draped pavilion shelters the sacred flames and hosts seasonal ceremonies. The priesthood begins to organize here, strengthening spiritual bonds.
Priests Hut
A permanent wooden hut for the high priest or priestess, who tends the sacred flame and interprets omens. The clergy gains authority among the people.
Sacred Flame Chamber
A timber-and-earth structure houses the eternal flame, watched day and night. Pilgrims journey here, deepening the faiths influence.
Sanctified Hall
A grand wooden hall, adorned with sacred carvings, where the greatest feasts and rites are held. The faiths power unites the clans.
Ancestors Shrine
A revered chamber lined with ancestor totems and offerings, honoring the spirits of those who came before. The communitys devotion deepens.
Holy Fire Room
A fortified chamber with stone hearths holds the most powerful flame, tended only by chosen elders. Pilgrimages from afar increase the shrines prestige.
Baltic Fire Sanctuary
A vast and awe-inspiring sanctuary of timber, stone, and sacred flame, where all the clans gather for the greatest festivals. The unity of the faithful is unbreakable.
